thread:
maria: Heads-up — reproduced a race where route-level quotas + scoped roles plus our authz cache let a revoked admin continue calling for ~25s. Not great for compliance. Anyone own invalidation behavior?
ryan: We're caching an 'effective_perms' blob per (subject, tenant) with a 30s TTL to avoid repeated policy evals.
oliver: That 30s was a pragmatic perf tradeoff but yea, enterprise customers will want near-instant revocation.
lia: UX note: when an admin clicks 'revoke' in the console they expect immediate effect or at least a clear modal that says 'revocation may take up to X seconds'. We should offer a stronger enforcement mode.
sam: Implementation options: 1) lower TTL globally (costly), 2) event-driven invalidation (push invalidation to nodes), 3) include policy-version in tokens and have gateway check it (requires token refresh), 4) per-route sticky quick-check for edge cases.
ryan: Prefer event-driven invalidation. We already emit audit events when role bindings change; extend that to an invalidation stream consumed by edge services. Concern: fanout at scale and ordering.
oliver: Agree event stream is cleanest. Minimal events: role_binding.add/remove, role.definition.update, scoped_token.revoke, service_account.key.rotate. Anything else?
maria: Also quota policy updates that change route limits should invalidate cached decision for routes impacted.
lia: From a rollout/console perspective could we add a 'force invalidate' button on binding detail pages? An admin could click it to push immediate invalidation and we can show a confirmation toast.
sam: We can surface two modes in console: 'Soft revocation (default)' and 'Force revoke (immediate)'. Force triggers async invalidation + telemetry ping to confirm nodes have dropped the cache.
ryan: Telemetry idea: perms-bot could emit back a short status when invalidation completes: "invalidation_ack: 42 nodes". That helps audits.
perms-bot: NOTE: invalidation events will be recorded in audit logs. Payload example: `{"event":"invalidate_permissions","tenant_id":"t-123","subject":"u-456","reason":"role_revoked","ts":1633036800}`
oliver: API surface: control-plane emits events to pubsub. Edge subscribes and applies invalidation either by key or by tenant prefix. We'll also support wildcard invalidation for when a role def changes (invalidate all subjects with role X).
maria: Security concern: make sure invalidation events are signed and authz for the invalidation stream is restricted; otherwise a compromised service could trigger mass revokes.
sam: Ops impact: we should offer a per-tenant 'revocation-strictness' flag (default false) so high-compliance tenants can require immediate enforcement and accept throughput cost. That can be toggled in the enterprise settings page.
lia: UX microcopy: toggle label suggestion: "Revocation strictness — immediate enforcement (may increase latency)" and a tooltip explaining costs. Also add a small banner the first time they enable it.
ryan: Edge implementation detail: when receiving invalidate_permissions for subject S, we should mark cache entry stale and evict. For wildcard invalidation (role X), compute affected entries via index or emit owner list in event. Computing on demand could be expensive.
oliver: We can emit two flavors: targeted invalidation (subject ids) and role-based invalidation (role id + optional affected_subjects list). Role edits trigger a targeted fanout from control-plane that resolves members.
maria: Can we gate the heavy fanout behind a background job to avoid control-plane latency? Emit job_id and then job emits chunked invalidation events; console shows progress.
sam: Sounds good. Also add a short-lived per-tenant policy-version header we bump on writes. Gateways check header vs cached version and treat mismatch as miss. That avoids full fanout for some cases.
ryan: Good hybrid: bump policy_version on writes and also emit invalidation events. Edge does fast check on header, and processes events for full consistency.
perms-bot: ACTION: create RFC draft: invalidation event schema, pubsub contract, console UX for force-revoke and tenant toggle, telemetry ack format. Tagging owners: @ryan (infra), @oliver (authz), @lia (product UX).
maria: I'll draft the RFC this afternoon and add a small PoC for the perms-bot ack messages. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
